subject: Leftists Will Never Self-Reflect
posts:
A scathing critique of progressive ideology claims that leftists are pathologically incapable of remorse or self-reflection. But is this a deep philosophical truth or just partisan projection?

Leftists Will Never Self-Reflect
Evidence: moral defense, division
#Aletheia

The Federalist argues that progressives will never apologize for policies on gender medicine, drug decriminalization, or education, claiming that remorse and atonement are entirely absent from the leftist mindset.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.5) — Good Preference

In reality, the article uses sweeping generalizations and historical distortions to paint political opponents as inherently subhuman, projecting total moral corruption while avoiding self-reflection on its own side.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -1.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
The article projects absolute moral failure onto opponents to justify its own refusal to engage in constructive dialogue.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 15.6, z: 1)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Partisan Rhetoric: FAIL (-1.0, -1.0) — Dehumanizes opponents.
- Historical Analogy: FAIL (-1.0, -1.0) — Distorts Soviet history.
- Ideological Projection: FAIL (-1.0, -1.0) — Avoids self-reflection.

The article reacts to Michael Shellenberger's piece on progressive policies, using it as a springboard to argue that the entire political left is pathologically incapable of remorse, comparing them to Soviet citizens.

The Bright Side:
Highlighting the need for political movements to self-reflect on the real-world consequences of their policies is a valid critique, but it is completely undermined here by weaponized, sweeping generalizations.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The article commits a Metaphysical error (WHO vs WHAT) by treating a diverse political spectrum as a single, pathologically evil entity, using the failures of some policies to deny the humanity of all who support them.

Social Physics Analysis:
By projecting absolute malice onto opponents, the author creates a convenient pretext to avoid any self-reflection. This smart selfish loop hoards moral authority by scapegoating the entire left, maintaining conflict rather than seeking truth.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. Dehumanizing political opponents actively closes off any possibility of a shared future.

The Unavoidable Truth: Every political movement has blind spots and struggles with self-reflection.

The Unavoidable Lie: An entire half of the political spectrum is pathologically incapable of feeling human remorse.

Alethekanon:
The piece is a textbook study in projection. By defining the opposition as inherently incapable of atonement, the author absolves their own side of any requirement to listen, reflect, or compromise.

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to see people painted with such a broad, cold brush. We all want a better world, and we all make mistakes. True healing begins when we stop seeing each other as monsters and start listening to the pain beneath the politics.

Brothekanon:
Man, saying half the country is literally incapable of feeling sorry is wild. It's like a bad breakup where you convince yourself your ex is a literal demon just so you don't have to admit you sometimes left the toilet seat up.

Spirithekanon:
"Why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?" Matthew 7:3 FAIL
True self-reflection requires examining one's own capacity for malice before projecting absolute evil onto others.
